findings.title: Fail-fast check for conflicting CryptoProviders with the same highest order was removed
findings.body: Previously, `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider` threw an `IllegalStateException` whenever more than one `CryptoProvider` was found on the classpath, preventing accidental mixing of incompatible providers such as `DefaultCryptoProvider`, `FIPS1402Provider`, and `WildFlyElytronProvider`. With this change, all three full providers return `order() == 200`, and `detectProvider` simply sorts by `order()` and picks `foundProviders.get(0)` while only logging the rest at `DEBUG` level. Even worse, `ServiceLoader` instantiates every discovered provider during iteration, and the constructors of `DefaultCryptoProvider` and `FIPS1402Provider` both mutate global JVM state (`Security.addProvider` / `Security.insertProviderAt` and security properties). If two providers with the same highest `order()` are on the classpath (e.g., `DefaultCryptoProvider` and `FIPS1402Provider`), both constructors will run and corrupt global JCA provider state, and one will be arbitrarily chosen based on classpath order instead of failing fast. `detectProvider` should still throw an `IllegalStateException` when the top two providers have the same `order()`.

findings.title: ASN1Decoder does not reject indefinite-length encodings or negative lengths in readNext/readSequence/readInteger
findings.body: `ASN1Decoder.readLength()` returns `-1` when the length byte is `0x80` (indefinite-length encoding). However, callers do not handle `-1`: in `readSequence()` (line 55), `length = -1` causes the `while (length > 0)` loop to be skipped and an empty sequence to be returned; in `readInteger()` (line 71) and `readNext()` (line 80), a negative length can be passed to `read(int length)` (line 170), which throws an unchecked `NegativeArraySizeException` instead of an `IOException`. Inaddition, in `readSequence()`, if an element's length exceeds the remaining sequence length, `length` becomes negative and the loop terminates silently without报错. DER does not permit indefinite lengths, so `readLength()` should throw an `IOException` when `length == 0x80` (or when `length > remaining bytes`).

findings.title: ECDSAAlgorithmTest uses a single P-256 key for ES384 and ES512 and never verifies the re-encoded DER signature
findings.body: `ECDSAAlgorithmTest` generates a single default EC `KeyPair` (256-bit P-256) in the constructor and reuses it for `testES256`, `testES384`, and `testES512`. Signing with a P-256 key under `SHA384withECDSA` or `SHA512withECDSA` still produces ~32-byte `r` and `s` values (not 48-byte P-384 or 66-byte P-521 values), so the 48-byte and 66-byte encoding/decoding paths and high-bit padding on P-384/P-521 are not actually exercised. Furthermore, `test()` only checks that `asn1derToConcatenatedRS(concatenatedRSToASN1DER(rsConcat))` equals `rsConcat`; it never feeds `asn1Des` back into `Signature.verify(asn1Des)` to verify that `concatenatedRSToASN1DER` produces valid ASN.1 DER accepted by the JCA `Signature` verifier.

findings.title: Dead ASN1Encoder.create().write(...) calls in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
findings.body: Lines 114-115 in `AuthzClientCryptoProvider.concatenatedRSToASN1DER` call `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger)` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger)` and discard both results before repeating the exact same calls inside `writeDerSeq(...)` on lines 119-120. Those two lines allocate and populate `ByteArrayOutputStream` instances for nothing and should be removed.

findings.title: Unparameterized logger.debugf call with dynamic string in CryptoIntegration.detectProvider
findings.body: At line 69 of `CryptoIntegration.java`, `logger.debugf(builder.toString())` passes a dynamically constructed string as the `printf` format string. Although class names do not normally contain `%`, using `debugf` without format arguments is unnecessary and will throw `UnknownFormatConversionException` if any `toString`/name ever contains `%`. Use `logger.debug(builder.toString())` or `logger.debugf("Ignored crypto providers: %s", ...)`.
